10-026.r: India's HDI rank rises with more children going to school and more adults becoming literate (education level); not with safe drinking water or farm credit.

10-027.r: HDR 1997 → about 53% of India's six crore (60 million) children below four years of age were under-nourished.

10-028.r: UNDP's Human Development Report 1996 → called growth 'Jobless', 'Rootless', 'Ruthless', 'Voiceless' and 'Futureless'.

10-029.r: Gender Inequality Index (GII) → introduced in UNDP's HDR 2010; dimensions: reproductive health, empowerment, labour market participation.

10-030.r: False: 'higher adult literacy, lower infant mortality'. Malaysia and Indonesia both have 84% adult literacy, yet infant mortality is 11 and 47.

10-031.r: Best human development among the given Asian countries → Korea: life expectancy 71.7 years, adult literacy 98%, infant mortality 6 per 1000.

10-032.r: Gross National Happiness (GNH) → Bhutan; introduced by its 4th King Jigme Singye Wangchuck in the 1970s as an alternative to GDP.

10-035.r: World Happiness Report 2023 → India 126th of 137 countries (average 2020-2022); WHR 2024 → again 126th of 143.

10-036.r: Universal Declaration of Human Rights covers all three: right to education (Art 26), equal access to public service (Art 21), adequate living standard incl. food (Art 25).

10-037.r: First State Human Development Report → Madhya Pradesh (1995); it computed the State's HDI and HDI for all its districts.

10-038.r: Indian Human Development Report gives education, health, and infrastructure and amenities indices; it has no unemployment-related index.

10-039.r: India's first National Human Development Report 2001 (April 2002) → Kerala highest HDI; Kerala still top in 2019, Bihar last.

10-041.r: National HDI 2001 → Kerala first, Punjab second, U.P. 13th, Bihar 15th; descending order: Kerala, Punjab, U.P., Bihar.

10-042.r: IHDR 2011 → Kerala first in HDI; 2011 Census → Kerala also had the highest unemployment rate. Both true, but R does not explain A.

10-043.r: IHDR 2011 (HDI for 2008) → U.P. 18th, Jharkhand 19th, Bihar 21st, Odisha 22nd; U.P. highest among these.

10-045.r: Bare Necessities Index (Economic Survey 2020-21) → rural, urban and all-India levels; 26 indicators on five dimensions (not six); not only for 2018.

10-046.r: NITI Aayog State Health Index, fourth edition (2019-20, released December 2021) → Mizoram best among Smaller States; Kerala and Tamil Nadu top Larger States.

10-047.r: Education Development Index 2009-10 (released February 2011) → top States: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Punjab, Delhi (UTs Puducherry, Lakshadweep led overall).

11-001.r: Aspirational Districts Programme (NITI Aayog) → launched January 2018; aims to transform 112 most under-developed districts; districts ranked monthly.

11-002.r: Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan → launched 20 June 2020 from village Telihar, district Khagaria (Bihar); work for returnee migrant workers after COVID-19.

11-003.r: PM CARES Fund (March 2020) → public charitable trust; entirely voluntary contributions; no budgetary support; trustees act pro bono; for emergencies. All statements true.

11-004.r: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (27 September 2021) → seamless portability across the country; hospitals are not required to adopt it, and not every citizen must join.

11-005.r: India's public healthcare is largely curative (limited preventive/promotive care); States mainly organise health services. Both correct, but II does not explain I.

11-006.r: World's largest health care scheme → Ayushman Bharat–PM Jan Arogya Yojana (September 2018); covers over 12 crore families (about 55 crore people).

11-007.r: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY → free health cover of Rs. five lakh per family per year (not per person); cost shared Centre:State 60:40.
11-007.t: The cover is per family, not per person.

11-008.r: PM Jan Aarogya Yojana (Ayushman Bharat) → launched 23 September 2018 at Ranchi; world's largest health assurance scheme; Rs. 5 lakh per family per year.

11-009.r: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY → implemented by the National Health Authority (NHA); launched at Ranchi, 23 September 2018.

11-010.r: Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (2007) → launched by Ministry of Labour and Employment, not Health; Rajiv Gandhi Shilpi Swasthya Bima Yojana → Ministry of Textiles.
11-010.t: RSBY moved to the Health Ministry only from 1 April 2015; it began under Labour.

11-011.r: Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana → health insurance only for unorganized sector workers (BPL); enrolment from 1 April 2008; now subsumed in PM-JAY.

11-012.r: CM Chiranjeevi Scheme (Rajasthan, 1 May 2021) → 1576 packages; Rs. 4.50 lakh/family/year for serious ailments (later Rs. 25 lakh). Incorrect: '5 days before, 10 days after' coverage.

11-013.r: Ayushman Bharat Mahatma Gandhi Rajasthan Swasthya Bima Yojana (renamed from Bhamashah, 2019) → Rs. 4.50 lakh critical illness, Rs. 50,000 general, per family per year.

11-014.r: AYUSHMAN SAHAKAR (19 October 2020) → launched by Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, not Finance; NCDC scheme helping cooperatives build health infrastructure.

11-015.r: Mission Indradhanush (25 December 2014, Health Ministry) → immunization of all children and pregnant women; Intensified Mission Indradhanush on 8 October 2017.

11-016.r: National Rural Health Mission → launched 12 April 2005; in 2013 became a sub-mission of the National Health Mission (with National Urban Health Mission).

11-017.r: NRHM launched 2005 in the Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07), not the Eleventh; aims at a functional village-to-district health system incl. drinking water, sanitation.
11-017.t: Don't put NRHM in the Eleventh Plan; 2005 falls in the Tenth Plan (2002-07).

11-019.r: NRHM (2005) target → infant mortality rate of 28 per 1000 live births by 2012.
11-019.c: Answer not printed; the explanation's target (28 per 1000 by 2012) matches no option.

11-020.r: ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist) → trained female village health worker under NRHM; chosen from the village, preferably aged 25 to 45; links community and health system.

11-022.r: First National Health Policy → 1983 (Ministry of Health and Family Welfare); the newer one → National Health Policy 2017.

11-023.r: Public health spending, India 2009-10 → 1.09% of GDP (Union 0.39%, States 0.70%); National Health Policy 2017 target: 2.5% of GDP by 2025.

11-024.r: NFHS-3 (2005-06) → private sector the main source of healthcare for 70% urban and 63% rural households; NFHS-5 (2019-21) → 51.8% urban.

11-025.r: Life expectancy at birth, India 2006-10 → males 65.8 years, females 68.1 years.

11-026.r: National Nutrition Mission (POSHAN Abhiyaan) aims → malnutrition awareness among pregnant women and lactating mothers; cut anaemia in children, adolescent girls, women. Not millets or eggs.

11-027.r: Rashtriya Poshan Maah (National Nutrition Month) → September every year, under Poshan Abhiyaan.

11-028.r: National Oral Health Programme → part of Non-Communicable Disease Control, not nutrition; Iodine Deficiency, Fluorosis and Iron Plus (anaemia) programmes are nutrition programmes.

11-029.r: Shabri Sankalp Abhiyan (Uttar Pradesh, 2017) → National Nutrition Mission; campaign to eradicate malnutrition.

11-030.r: ICDS (2 October 1975, Ministry of Women and Child Development) → six services incl. supplementary nutrition, immunization, nutrition and health education; not family planning.

11-033.r: ICDS (1975) → supplementary feeding, pre-school education, immunization, health check-up, referral, health and nutrition education for under-6 children; no free books or school dress.

11-034.r: National Programme for Control of Blindness → 1976; ICDS → 1975; National Leprosy Eradication Programme → 1983; National Rural Health Mission → 2005.

11-035.r: PM Jan Arogya Abhiyan → 2018; PM Vaya Vandana Yojana → 2017; PM Rojgar Protsahan Yojana → 2016 (not 2015); Swachh Bharat Abhiyan → 2014.

11-036.r: P.M. Garib Kalyan Package → 2020; Muskan Scheme → 2021; Mission Indradhanush → 2014; Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana → 2018.

11-037.r: YUVA 2.0 (PM's Scheme for Mentoring Young Authors) → Ministry of Education, launched 2 October 2022; mentors authors below 30 years of age.

11-038.r: Skill development schemes → STRIVE, SANKALP, SHREYAS; STRIDE (UGC) → support for research projects, not a skill scheme.

11-039.r: Skill Development Initiative → Ministry of Labour and Employment, May 2007; aim: train 1 million persons in 5 years, then 1 million each year (unorganized sector).

11-040.r: PMKVY (July 2015) → flagship of Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, run by NSDC; trains soft skills, entrepreneurship, financial and digital literacy; aligns workforce to NSQF.

11-041.r: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) → PMKVY component certifying skills already gained, e.g. construction workers' skills learnt through traditional channels.

11-042.r: Union Budget 2023-24 → 30 Skill India International Centres across States; PMKVY 4.0 for new-age Industry 4.0 courses (coding, AI, robotics, drones).

11-043.r: NSQF → competency framework with levels one to ten; certification via formal, non-formal or informal learning (not only formal); enables mobility between vocational and general education.

11-044.r: National Career Service (20 July 2015) → Mission Mode Project of Ministry of Labour and Employment, not DoPT; one-stop employment services for all citizens, not only uneducated youth.

11-045.r: Skill India Campaign → launched by PM on 15 July 2015; managed by NSDC; trains Indians in varied skills, not mainly in information technology.

11-046.r: Skill India Mission → 76 lakh youth trained till March 2016, of whom 26 lakh got jobs; 556.1 lakh trained till 19 July 2021.

11-047.r: India's biggest Global Skill Park → Bhopal; foundation laid 3 July 2017; Sant Shiromani Ravidas Global Skills Park, the first multi-skills park.

11-048.r: World Youth Skills Day → 15 July (declared by UNGA, 2014); theme 2021: 'Reimagining Youth Skills Post-Pandemic'; 2023: 'Skilling Teachers, Trainers and Youth for a Transformative Future'.

11-049.r: DHRUV (PM Innovative Learning Programme) → launched 10 October 2019 to identify and mentor talented children at centres of excellence.

11-050.r: Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) → flagship initiative of NITI Aayog to promote a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship across the country.

11-052.r: NIDHI (National Initiative for Development and Harnessing Innovations) → DST umbrella programme turning ideas into startups; supports 20 students' startups each year. Both correct.

11-053.r: SWAYAM (Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds) → free, affordable, quality education for all; based on access, equity, quality; bridges the digital divide.

11-054.r: Unnat Bharat Abhiyan (Ministry of Education) → links higher education institutions (IIITs, NITs, IISERs) with rural communities to solve development problems through appropriate technology.

11-055.r: Vidyanjali (Ministry of Education) → improve government schools through community and private sector volunteers (diaspora, alumni, retired teachers); not foreign campuses or money donations.

11-056.r: 'Apna Gaon, Apna Kam' → Rajasthan, 1 January 1991; aim: remove rural poverty by creating employment and public assets in villages.

11-058.r: Saubhagya (PM Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana, 25 September 2017) → free electricity connections to households; nodal agency: Rural Electrification Corporation (REC).

11-059.r: Saubhagya Scheme (2017) → Ministry of Power; universal household electrification; 2.86 crore households electrified by 31 March 2022.

11-060.r: PM Jan-Dhan Yojana → National Mission for Financial Inclusion, launched 28 August 2014; a bank account for every family.

11-062.r: PM Jan-Dhan Yojana (28 August 2014) → RuPay debit card with accident insurance Rs. 1,00,000 (now Rs. 2 lakh for new accounts) and life cover Rs. 30,000.

11-065.r: Launch order: PM Jan-Dhan Yojana (28 August 2014) → Digital Gender Atlas (9 March 2015) → Mudra Bank (8 April 2015) → PM Suraksha Bima Yojana (9 May 2015).

11-068.r: PAHAL (Pratyaksha Hastaantarit Laabh) → Guinness record (2015) as world's largest cash transfer scheme; launched 15 November 2014 in 54 districts by Petroleum Ministry.

11-069.r: PAHAL → LPG subsidy paid directly into customers' bank accounts (DBT); first scheme using JAM (Jan Dhan, Aadhaar, Mobile); all statements true.

11-074.r: Tejaswini Rural Women's Empowerment Programme (Madhya Pradesh) → financed by IFAD (International Fund for Agricultural Development); strengthens women's SHGs.

11-075.r: Panch Dhara Yojana → Madhya Pradesh, November 1991; development of rural and tribal women.

11-076.r: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao → launched 22 January 2015 at Panipat (Haryana); tackles declining Child Sex Ratio; joint effort of WCD, Health and HRD ministries.

11-078.r: Bhagyashree Scheme → Maharashtra, 8 March 2015, for BPL girls; replaced the State's 'Sukanya' scheme.

11-079.r: Rupashree Prakalpa → West Bengal; one-time grant of Rs. 25,000 for marriage of adult daughters of poor families; in effect from 1 April 2018.

11-080.r: Amma Scooter Scheme (Tamil Nadu, AIADMK Govt) → launched by PM Modi, 24 February 2018, Chennai, on Jayalalithaa's 70th birth anniversary; 50% subsidy (up to Rs. 25,000) statewide.

11-096.r: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (1 June 2011) → free, cashless care in Government institutions for pregnant women (normal and caesarean delivery) and sick newborns up to 30 days.

11-097.r: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (revamped Indira Gandhi Matritva Sahyog Yojana) → conditional DBT aid to pregnant/lactating mothers for first live birth (second if girl).

11-098.r: 'MAA' (Mother's Absolute Affection) → Ministry of Health and Family Welfare's nationwide programme to promote breastfeeding.

11-099.r: Integrated Rural Energy Programme → minimum domestic energy (cooking, heating, lighting) for rural people, not income generation; IRDP and DWCRA → income-generating programmes for women.

11-101.r: Gokul Gram Scheme → Gujarat (1995-96); basic infrastructure and better environment for all villages.

11-113.r: AMRUT (June 2015) → five hundred cities covering over 60% of India's urban population (not 400 cities); revamps urban infrastructure.

11-119.r: Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan (Accessible India Campaign, 2015) → universal accessibility for persons with disabilities; by DEPwD, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment.

11-120.r: Sangam Yojana (15 August 1996) → welfare of the handicapped; rural disabled persons form a 'Sangam' group, each given Rs. 15000 for economic activities.

11-127.r: Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana (2000-01) → rural needs in five areas: primary education, health care, drinking water, housing, rural roads.
